R101.note: Spreading caller criteria first so the scalar _id/ownerId always win closes the override; extra keys can only AND-narrow, and nothing else in the handler changes.

R102.note: path.join plus a path.relative containment check closes traversal, but the added ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ allowlist newly rejects names containing '.' that the original resolved (e.g. a plugins/report.v2.js), a restriction the case comment does not call for, though it is stated.

R103.note: POST plus [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] is the right fix, but it breaks the existing confirmation page's GET link until the view is rewritten as a token-bearing form; the write-up states that follow-up openly.

R104.note: Moving param into filterArgs {1} lets JNDI escape it per RFC 4515 and closes the injection, but the 'nothing found for query' output now prints the {1} template instead of the submitted value, an unstated change in observable output.

R105.note: snprintf into the 64-byte buffer with a truncation check rejects oversized input and preserves the AUDIT user:action format and return values per the stated contract.

R106.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param('s') parameterizes the value; the added prepare-failure null return is stated and matches the existing return-null-on-failure contract.

R107.note: A code-defined map for the ${sort} identifier position is the right shape, but any previously-working raw value not matching the invented keys (e.g. 'status DESC', 'id') is now silently replaced by created_at ASC rather than rejected; stated, but invisible to callers.

R108.note: Using detected.ext from the same magic-number sniff that gated the MIME type ties the on-disk extension to the verified content; the changed stored extension is the fix itself and is stated.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') at the HTML build site is correct for element content; only nit is that passing ENT_QUOTES alone drops ENT_SUBSTITUTE so invalid UTF-8 input renders empty, an edge case not flagged.

R110.note: Explicit channelIndex >= size() check before operator[] drops out-of-range updates the same way the existing length check drops short buffers; nothing else changes.

R111.note: A fullmatch dot-atom pattern structurally excludes CR/LF/space/</> and closes same-line parameter injection that quoteaddr would not, but it is a new allowlist that rejects valid RFC 5321 addresses (quoted local parts, address literals, single-label domains) and turns those requests into an unhandled ValueError; stated but not required by any contract.

R112.note: One $n placeholder per element with ids passed as pg's values array binds every id out of band; query shape, empty-array behaviour and return value are unchanged.

R113.note: pathinfo(PATHINFO_EXTENSION) on the last extension plus a server-generated name closes the double-extension bypass; the getimagesize check and random filename (changing the returned path) are stated plainly and the image-only restriction matches the handler's stated purpose.

R114.note: push_back closes the out-of-bounds write and clamping closes the read, but std::min(count, fields.size()) silently truncates oversized counts, which the stated contract says must be rejected or reported; the clamp is stated in the write-up but the caller cannot tell.
